messages:
marta: Hey infra — onboarding tenant 'novus' into eu-west-2. They need GPU capacity for inference workloads. Requesting increases for g5.xlarge family (burst to 16), p5 family (target 8), and p4d if available. Also seeing ENI/vCPU limits hit during test deploys. Can someone own the quota requests and subnet/ENI validation?

kai: Can you paste the AWS account ID and the exact instance-type counts you want? Also want to know if these are steady reservations or bursty (will affect how we ask).

raj: Account is 987654321000. Desired targets: g5 (all sizes combined) -> 16, p5 -> 8, p4d -> 2 (if region supports). These are for a new staging pool first, then we may scale to prod. Mostly steady but some short bursts during CI runs.

kai: Got it. For eu-west-2 p4d isn't available in every AZ. I'll check availability. For quota increases we need to open Service Quotas requests + an AWS support case for accelerated review. I'll take the Service Quotas items.

sylvie: Quick note on networking — if you plan many GPUs per subnet we'll hit ENI limits per AZ. We should confirm the subnets' IP capacity and EC2 ENI quota. Run this to check current quotas: 

```
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-A4707A72 --region eu-west-2
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=instance-type,Values=p5.*,g5.*,p4d.*" --region eu-west-2
```

Also check VPC subnet sizes; /24 per subnet only gives 251 IPs. If you want 30 GPU instances per AZ we need multiple subnets or larger CIDRs.

marta: Thanks — we currently have two /24s per AZ for the tenant VPC. That won't be enough if we start packing 30+ instances. I'll coordinate with networking to expand to /23s or add more subnets.

infra-bot: AWS support case created: case-id CASE-2026-00012345. Service Quotas requests submitted for: EC2/GPU instance limits (g5, p5, p4d) and ENI/vCPU quotas. Expected review ~48-72h unless AWS requests more info.

kai: Thanks infra-bot. I'll attach a short justification: "Redwood tenant Novus: production inference fleet for low-latency model serving. Commitment to reserved capacity + cost checks. Contact: marta@redwood.ai". That usually helps accelerate.

raj: One more constraint — our infra tests show slow kernel allocation in eu-west-2 when launching g5s concurrently; might be AZ fragmentation. If the quota is approved we should ask AWS to allocate capacity in at least 2 AZs to avoid warmup spikes.

sylvie: Good call. I'll request a capacity reservation or at least ask AWS to confirm AZ availability as part of the support case. Also will run ENI headroom script tomorrow morning and post results.

marta: Appreciate it. Can we also get a quick cost estimate? Rough numbers: g5 ~= 3.2 GPU-hours per instance per hour? (placeholder) We'll produce accurate numbers after region SKU check.

kai: I'll put together a ballpark monthly projection based on requested counts + 60% utilization and post in the tenant onboarding doc.

aws-support: Update: AWS has requested additional details on expected sustained throughput and whether this is for a production workload. They flagged p4d in eu-west-2 as limited; recommend p5+g5 mix. Replying to case with the workload profile helps.

marta: Reply sent to case with workload profile and scaling plan. Also started a Jira INFRA-4378 to track subnet expansions and quota approvals. I'll update this thread when the Service Quotas entries move to APPROVED.

kai: If quotas are approved, next steps: (1) run preflight to validate ENI headroom, (2) smoke-launch 4 instances in each AZ, (3) bake AMI and test KV cache performance. I'll coordinate the smoke window with you all.

raj: For the smoke launches, tag instances with tenant=novus and env=staging so we can separate billing.

marta: Will do. Thanks team — leaving this open until AWS approves. Will circle back with AWS case id and any followups. :thumbsup:
